title: What If It Snowed in the Sahara? It Already Has

scenes.text: What if it snowed in the Sahara Desert? It already has, and satellites caught it.
The first recorded Sahara snowfall came in 1979. It has happened again since, including in 2016 and 2018.
In January 2018, satellites saw snow near Aïn Séfra in northern Algeria, on high ground above 1,000 meters.
NASA says about 10 to 30 centimeters fell, roughly 4 to 12 inches, on the orange dunes.
But it never lasts. In every significant case, the snow melted within hours as temperatures climbed.
So the world's biggest hot desert can turn white. It just can't stay that way.
